1. Pension Credit (Guarantee Credit) - rules PC-1 to PC-5.
- PC-1: Claimant must live in England, Scotland, or Wales and have reached State Pension age. Facts: country = Wales (F3, F18), age 85 > state pension age 66 (F22, F23). So condition met.
- PC-2: Claimant must include partner; both partners must have reached State Pension age. Facts: has_partner = no (F4, F15, F20). So no partner, condition met (since no partner to include).
- PC-3: Savings up to £10,000 ignored; above that, every £500 or part thereof counts as £1 weekly income. Savings = 0 (F11). So no savings income.
- PC-4: Guarantee Credit tops up weekly income to £238 (single) or £363.25 (couple); eligible if assessed income below threshold. Since single, threshold £238. Assessed weekly income = weekly_income_total + savings income. Weekly income total = £237.99 (F6, F13). Savings income = 0. So assessed income = £237.99, which is below £238. So eligible.
- PC-5: Weekly Guarantee Credit amount is the difference between threshold and assessed weekly income. Difference = £238 - £237.99 = £0.01 per week. So weekly amount = £0.01.

But wait: The rule says "eligible if assessed income below threshold." Since £237.99 < £238, eligible. Weekly amount = difference = £0.01. However, the rule says "If every condition is met but only the rate is unclear, the household is eligible: give the lower rate." Here rate is clear: difference. So weekly_amount = 0.01.

- AA-1: Must have reached State Pension age. Yes, age 85 > 66.

For those not on Guarantee Credit, the reduction is calculated as per CTR-6. Since her income is below applicable amount, she gets full weekly net charge as reduction, i.e., 100% reduction. Since income below applicable amount, reduction = 32.61826923. We'll round to two decimals: 32.62.

But note: The rule says "The applicable amount is the Pension Credit guarantee amount (£238 single, £363.25 couple)." That's the same as PC threshold. So indeed.

Thus council_tax_reduction: eligible, weekly_amount = 32.62.
